evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository (domain ports), so these are pure persistence adapters.

src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts: OrderController is constructor-injected with CatalogueService and OrderService, and every route calls a service method (addProduct, placeOrder, advanceOrder, cancelOrder, and so on). It never calls a repository directly.

src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts: stateFrom validates against the domain's orderStates instead of keeping its own copy of the list, and handle() is the only place that maps NotFoundError/DomainError/other errors to 404/409/500.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: createServer() is a composition root. It builds InMemoryProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository, passes them to the services and mounts OrderController.routes().

Minor: in src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts the parameter type of transition(target: 'paid' | 'packed' | 'shipped' | 'delivered') repeats part of the domain order-state list, and idFrom throws DomainError for a transport-level check. Neither breaks the module's cohesion.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files are infrastructure adapters for the order fulfilment API. in-memory-repositories.ts holds the persistence adapters, which implement the domain interfaces ProductRepository and OrderRepository. order-controller.ts is the HTTP adapter: it hands every request to CatalogueService and OrderService and never touches repositories or domain entities directly. server.ts is the composition root that wires the adapters to the services. The module's abstractions are used consistently. The controller never bypasses the services, and server.ts builds everything through constructors. Each rule lives in one place. State validation in stateFrom reuses the domain's orderStates rather than copying the list, and HTTP error mapping is kept in the single handle() wrapper. Three small points are not violations. OrderController also serves the /products routes. idFrom reports a missing route id with DomainError, so the client gets a 409. The literal union in transition() ('paid' | 'packed' | 'shipped' | 'delivered') repeats part of the domain's state list. None of these splits the module into unrelated concerns or bypasses its abstractions.
